habitat 'water' with NO constId claimed. The engine's real answer is a per-object terrain-restriction id in the dat (preview-design Sec.15 item 23) and this is the interim stand-in, added 2026-08-08 because the alternative is worse rather than because the value is measured: an object the reference data does not know falls back to habitat 'land', so every fish a script placed without terrain_to_place_on stood on dry ground. Observed on QS_Three_Bays_v1.1.rms, where TUNA came out on the beach. Class evidence: the guide lists 905 OCEAN_FISH_CLASS beside 933 SHORE_FISH_CLASS, so the game itself separates deep-water fish from the shore family. The name is written bare in shipped scripts with no #const anywhere in the corpus, which is consistent with a predefined constant but does not prove one — the engine would pass an undefined name silently. Nothing here depends on that either way: objectHabitat resolves by rmsConstant, so the id is deliberately left null rather than guessed. No resourceAmounts either: the food yield is unmeasured here and requiresGaiaOnly reads that field, so inventing one would change gaia handling as a side effect.
